newsitem.title: FINLAND: Confusion delays planned pulp derivatives bourse.
newsitem.headline: Confusion delays planned pulp derivatives bourse.

text.p: The start-up of the world's first bourse to trade wood pulp derivatives has been delayed by confusion over who is entitled to participate, organiser Suomen Optioporssi Oy (SOP) said Thursday.
"We now plan to start before Christmas or in early December, as soon as we get enough participants," SOP Vice President Jaakko Soini told Reuters.

SOP's Finnish Options Exchange (FOEX), which will enable pulp buyers and sellers to hedge against steep swings in prices by trading in futures and options, was initially slated to begin trade in September.

But the project has been delayed by a recent ruling from Finland's Financial Supervision authority that Finnish banks and securities brokers were excluded from this sort of trading activity, Soini said.
Financial Supervision official Anne Jaakkola said commodities derivatives were not among instruments investment services companies are allowed to trade under Finnish law.
Soini said SOP found this interpretation surprising: "The attitude used to be that whatever was not expressly forbidden was allowed, but that doesn't seem to be the case this time."
But despite the delay, Soini said industry remains enthusiastic about the pulp futures bourse. @
"We aim to get 30 market participants. Now we have about 10 companies signed up," Soini said, adding that most were foreign companies although he declined to name them.
"The ruling does not apply to foreign licensed commodities brokers," he said.
He said the solution to the mix-up would be that instead of making a contract with a broker, companies would now participate directly on the bourse.
While trade could start with fewer than 30 participants, he said having fewer than 20 could put the market at risk of insufficient liquidity. @
"In principle we could start right now. We just need to have enough of a group so that we can consider trading to be on a firm footing and that it has a future," he said.

The unusual feature of SOP's planned fully electronic pulp in market pulp futures and options would be its settlement: in cash, without committing players to take physical delivery from a potentially unknown counterparty.

SOP has already begun providing the market with PIX pulp benchmark price information for Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft on Mondays on Reuters page SOPI. Information for calculating the price is supplied by more than 30 companies in 11 countries.
The October 7 price was $568.10 per tonne, up from an average of $562.13 in September.
Soini said there had been some talk of amending Finnish law to allow securities brokers to trade in commodities derivatives. "(But) I don't see anything happening in the short term."
